correctness.rationale: Direct neighbor count on one clique is a−x+y and degree n. For even n=2m this gives shore update ∅ if a<m, B if a=m, U if a>m. For odd n=2m+1 it gives ∅ if a<m, B\A if a=m, (U\A)∪B if a=m+1, U if a>m+1; the other shore follows symmetrically. The all-n partition by (a,b,c=|A∩B|) isolates all primitive 2-cycles and odd one-step preperiod states; extremal shores reach fixed configurations. Combinatorics yield even C=binom(2m,m): fixed 4+C, primitive period-2 orbits (C²−C)/2, basin C²−C; odd D=binom(2m+1,m): fixed 4, primitive orbits (m+2)D, basin 2(m²+2m+2)D, preperiodic period-two states 2m(m+1)D. Explicit boundary witnesses give max transients 1 (n=2), 2 (n=3 and even n≥4), 3 (odd n≥5). Independent all-labelled-state simulation for n=2,…,8 confirms update, periods, basins and max transients; the uniform case division—not finite extrapolation—proves all n. Stirling yields the claimed exact leading parity scales.
residual_risks: All labels are distinguished, and primitive orbits are quotient only by time shift, not by graph automorphism.
The nearest-pair edge counts must exclude the vertex’s own opinion and include its matched opposite, which the formula does.

value.rationale: Two highly cohesive communities coupled only by a perfect matching form a canonical regular graph family. The complete period-two orbit and attraction-basin census plus an exponential-versus-polynomial parity separation in oscillation probability is a significant dynamical distinction not predicted by eventual-period theorem alone.
residual_risks: The specific threshold rule and graph family are essential; no extension to asynchronous or weighted systems is proved.

final_claim: For every n≥2, synchronous tie-retaining binary majority on K_n □ K₂ has explicit fixed, primitive 2-cycle and basin counts, sharp maximum preperiod ≤3, and parity contrast p_even∼2/(πn) versus p_odd∼n^{3/2}2^{−n}/√(2π).
